title: Emma Banay:
title_short: Emma Banay · Why a funder pays for proof
headline: Kids lined up down the block at 8 AM on a Saturday. A funder explains why that demand needs evidence to match, and why fun and rigor can go together.
story: Emma is the Overdeck Family Foundation's portfolio manager for Learn Fresh. The first time she saw it, kids and families were lined up down the block at 8 AM on a Saturday.
That is the point: incredible demand, so the evidence of impact has to match. Her closing message: rigorous math learning doesn't have to come at the expense of student experience.

Loops: L1 “Why were kids lined up?” opens at 0:00 and closes at 0:11 (“kids want to play”). L2 “What does a funder need?” opens at 0:11 and closes at the button. Stakes: programs that are fun but unproven.

End on “really strong learning outcomes”, then the Learn more end card.
